description:
Project: Quickstart templates (RAG + agents). Redwood Inference is investing in production-minded onboarding assets that let developers go from “API key” to a working, observable application quickly—without teaching unsafe patterns. The scope is to ship a set of opinionated templates (primarily Python + TypeScript, with selective Go) covering (1) RAG service + ingestion pipeline, (2) agent-style orchestration with tool calling, and (3) combined RAG+agent workflows. Each template must include observability hooks (OpenTelemetry tracing, structured logs, request/tenant correlation IDs, cost/latency metrics, error taxonomy) and safe defaults (timeouts, retries/backoff, rate-limit handling, secrets management patterns, prompt/tool safety guardrails, and PII handling guidance). The templates must align with Redwood’s Hosted API and Console capabilities (token-level cost breakdowns, routing/fallback policies, rollout safety), and provide a clear path to Dedicated/Private deployment considerations.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-first-success for PLG users (target: <15 minutes to first successful run; <60 minutes to deploy to a managed environment).
- Provide “production shape” from day one: sane config layering, health checks, graceful shutdown, and baseline dashboards/alerts.
- Establish a stable template contract: consistent env vars, telemetry schema, error codes, and SDK usage patterns across languages.
- Improve supportability: templates should minimize common ticket drivers (streaming disconnects, missing retries/timeouts, misconfigured keys, noisy logs, and confusing 429 behavior).

Non-goals:
- Building a full framework or managed agent runtime.
- Supporting every vector DB / tool plugin out of the gate (start with 1–2 common backends and a clear extension interface).

Key stakeholders:
- Developer Experience: Alex Martinez (exec), Monica Patel (SDK), Elliot Price / Wei Chen (Docs), Renee Sullivan (Advocacy).
- Product: Nikhil Sharma (Hosted API), Marissa Cole / Paula Mendes (Console & rollouts), Henry Cho (API ergonomics).
- Platform/Telemetry: Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman, Allison Grant (observability standards).
- Security: Naomi Feldman (product), Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei (secure defaults).
- SRE: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes (operational guardrails, alert hygiene).

Phases & timeline (illustrative):
1) Discovery & requirements (2025-11 to 2025-12): inventory top onboarding failures from Support, align on template telemetry schema + safe defaults.
2) Design & contract definition (2025-12): decide template catalog, folder structure, env var contract, and dashboards.
3) Implementation (2025-12 to 2026-01): build templates in redwood-quickstarts + reference apps in redwood-examples; update SDK helpers; add CI.
4) Pilot & hardening (2026-01): internal dogfooding, community feedback, fix papercuts, tighten security guidance.
5) Launch (2026-02): docs-site integration, announcement, and ongoing maintenance ownership (DX + SDK + Docs).

Deliverables:
- Template repos (RAG, agents, combined) with local + containerized run paths.
- A minimal “observability pack” (dashboards/alerts + trace exemplars) that works out of the box.
- Documentation updates and a maintenance playbook (versioning, deprecations, release checklist).
- Work tracking via Linear projects; implementation via GitHub PRs; coordination via Slack; early drafts and metric sheets in Drive; support feedback loops via Jira.
